findings.observation: The architecture-freeze manifest explicitly protects the current controlled proof path and its required files.
findings.proposed_action: Treat manifest-required files and proven semantics as protected baseline. Expand to transitive dependency closure before any broad consolidation.

evidence: Repeated focus on pipeline/routes/rate edge and abnormal-path coverage
Sequential plan-number naming rather than stable behavior-domain naming
findings.observation: The ten sequential coverage-plan suites repeatedly exercise overlapping pipeline, replay-route, and rate-limiting abnormal branches. Sample inspection shows repeated fixtures and neighboring failure modes, but not every assertion is duplicate.
findings.proposed_action: Build a target-function/test-case matrix, then consolidate only exact or fixture-level duplication into behavior-oriented suites.

evidence: Function docstring explicitly labels it legacy SHA-256 integrity verification
Repository search found tests and review documentation
No supported runtime caller was found by the initial code-search pass
findings.observation: The legacy SHA-256 verifier may be removable if no runtime, CLI, packaging, or migration consumer remains.
findings.proposed_action: Confirm with static import/symbol reachability plus entry-point search. If zero supported consumers remain, deprecate/remove in a separate PR with policy-signing tests updated.

evidence: 31 Python files with trustlog/trust_log in path
findings.observation: There are multiple TrustLog verification surfaces, but initial evidence shows different ledger/CLI roles. Treating them as duplicates now would be unsafe.
findings.proposed_action: Create a role/ledger/consumer matrix before any verifier unification. Separate full encrypted ledger, signed witness/unified verifier, and script-local verification responsibilities.

evidence: Native v2 authorization/final-recheck code imports parts of these lineages
findings.observation: The parallel naming and large volume strongly justify consolidation review, but the frozen proof path currently depends on this lineage. Size or naming similarity is not evidence of removability.
findings.proposed_action: Compute frozen transitive dependency closure and packet responsibility matrix. Only then identify canonical/legacy pairs with behaviorally equivalent contracts.

evidence: Among the largest runtime Python modules
Used by API tests and the /v1/decide surface
findings.observation: The API schema module is large enough to merit boundary review, but it is connected to the actual decision route used by the frozen E2E proof.
findings.proposed_action: Map schema classes to API routes/clients/tests before considering a split. Prefer mechanical module split with compatibility imports only if consumer mapping shows low risk.

evidence: 471 test Python files versus 432 runtime Python files

Several very large coverage/ext suites: test_pipeline_stages_ext.py 277,589 bytes, test_server_api.py 182,859 bytes, test_fuji_gate.py 131,189 bytes, test_kernel_decide_ext.py 129,743 bytes, test_coverage_consolidated_ext.py 117,478 bytes
findings.observation: Test volume alone is not a defect, but coverage-driven extension suites are likely to contain fixture and scenario duplication that increases maintenance cost.
findings.proposed_action: Use AST/test-name/target-function grouping to find exact fixture and assertion overlap. Preserve distinct safety-boundary tests even when setup is similar.
